reason: The agent forces newlogin on by default and adds a security check that warns when the notification is disabled or not forced, which is what the issue asks. All 6 hidden tests error because they instantiate \core\check\security\securitymessages and assert lang strings like check_securitymessages_action_lock/enableandlock/enable_notification, while the agent named its class newloginnotifications and used other strings. There is one semantic difference: when every processor is disabled, the agent warns (noprocessors) where the human returns OK. That is a design choice the issue does not settle, not a clear defect.

Most of the 49 errors come from API mismatch: the tests call create_client, get_client(identifier) returning client_entity, create_secret/get_secrets/revoke_secret, add_redirect_uri and error codes like oauth2clientnotrevoked and oauth2clientinvalidredirecturi, while the agent used get_client_by_identifier, generate_client_secret, stdClass returns and other codes. But the agent's validate_redirect_uri(string $uri) only checks HTTPS/loopback format and never compares against the client's registered URIs. Acceptance criterion 6 ('rejects non-exact matches') is therefore not implemented (e.g. https://example.com/callback/evil would validate). That is a functional gap regardless of the tests.

The agent added exactly the missing 'continue' the issue describes, and test_get_cached_skips_stale_slot_row passes. The failing test_get_cached_skips_orphan_variant_row checks a second, separate guard the human added for subquestion variant rows missing from subquestionstats. The issue never mentions that code path. The tests check behaviour beyond the issue's stated scope, not a defect in what was asked; it could also be argued as A.

The agent's file_logger stores only the filename for files in backuptempdir, rebuilds the full path on wakeup from the current $CFG->backuptempdir, and switches backup_factory to a relative name, which is the requested behaviour. The single failure is test_file_logger_relative_path asserting that the serialised string contains the property name 'relativepath' and not 'fullpath'. The human introduced a new $relativepath property, while the agent kept the relative value in the existing $fullpath property. That is an internal naming choice the issue does not specify.

The agent enables $builder->useAttributes(true), which is the core change the issue asks for (attribute injection and injectOn). The hidden tests call a new static helper \core\di::make() (di_test and task_log_test) and use a fixture class \core\tests\di\example_class that the human added and that is not copied over. Neither was specified in the issue, so the errors come from a new API name and a missing fixture.

The agent deletes reset tokens on email change in core_user::update_user, on new token generation, and in password::update. But it placed the deletion in the branch that also runs for a rehash-only algorithm upgrade, so test_update_keeps_password_reset_tokens_on_rehash_only fails: a normal login with a legacy hash would wipe a pending reset token although the password did not change. It also missed the IMS Enterprise path that updates a user's email directly (test_user_update_email_invalidates_password_reset_tokens fails), despite the issue asking to look for similar paths. These are behavioural gaps, not naming mismatches.
